g.text: H-PAIRWORK and its fix: nine registrations, each written before the run it judges (scientific/14 §2)
1 · H-PAIRWORK
: is one comparison within the caps
below the long-task threshold of 50 ms? A(n), B, C, D,
predictions P1-P5, and what each outcome means
2 · design F
registered before it is written: visit only
what can match (F-a), count first (F-b), pack the cells (F-c).
Q1-Q4, and the cap rule if C > 16 ms
3 · H-FLOOD, H-FAR
: a design review attacks F's time.
Can crafted cells share one bucket of V8's number hash?
Can far cells fall back to string keys?
4 · design F′
: its own table, hashed at random per call,
amended BEFORE it is written: simple tabulation, not a
linear family (3-independent; Chernoff-type loads)
6 · design F″
, a deviation decided before code: group the
strings by a stable merge sort, no hash, and cap the text.
Q1″, Q2⁗, Q5, Q6 (the text cap by a rule), E1 (g)-(j)
7 · H-TEXT2
, written after Q6's result (it can only lower
the cap): two-byte and mixed-width strings join the rule
8 · H-COMBINED
: one page at all three caps at once:
a rule picks the text and match caps together, by the
smaller headroom
9 · the final F″
: every control fails where predicted,
E2 and E3 find nothing
